notes: The reference queues are driven by one level-sensitive process that detects both clock edges, so Q and P have a single driver. Assertions read NBA snapshots (s_*), so they see the state from before the current edge. At simultaneous edges the read is processed first. The word read at P-clear edge 5 is still checked against P, then P is cleared. A write accepted at the busy-rise edge is pushed to Q and then moved to P. CHK-006 has two assertions (write clock and read clock), so its hits are counted in the model process instead of an always_ff, which avoids a multi-clock driver on hits_CHK_006. I did not compile or simulate this against Verilator.
